quarterly payment system reports, over a benchmark of factual / numerical / trend /
multihop questions.

## Setup

```bash
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

```

You'll also need the [`tesseract`](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract) binary

install tesseract-ocr` on Linux).

```bash

```

## Add your data

   [rma.org.bt](https://www.rma.org.bt) and place the PDFs under:
   ```
   corpus/annual/*.pdf
   corpus/quarterly/*.pdf
   ```
2. **Benchmark** — fill in `benchmark/benchmark.csv` with your question set (the
   checked-in file has 5 example rows showing the expected schema):
   ```
   question_id,question,category,reference_answer,source_doc,source_page
   ```
   `category` must be one of: `factual`, `numerical`, `trend`, `multihop`.

## Run

Open `RMA_RAG_Benchmark.ipynb` and run top to bottom:

```bash
jupyter notebook RMA_RAG_Benchmark.ipynb
```

| Section | What it does |
|---|---|
| 0 | Install/import, API key check |
| 1 | Extract + OCR-fallback + clean the corpus, chunk it two ways (fixed-window, structure-aware) |
| 2 | Build the BM25 index and dense (`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`) embeddings |
| 3 | Retrieval functions: zero-context, BM25, dense, hybrid RRF |
| 4 | Generation via OpenRouter (`meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct`), with retry/backoff and artifact-regeneration |
| 5 | Runs every benchmark question through all 4 conditions → `results/results.csv` |
| 6 | ROUGE / BERTScore / no-answer-rate tables (Table 3, Table 4) |
| 7 | Interactive faithfulness annotation on a 20% sample of hybrid outputs |
| 8 | Figures: per-category ROUGE-L bar chart, abstention-vs-quality scatter |

Section 7 is interactive (`input()` prompts) — run it in a live kernel, not via
"Run All." It checkpoints after every row, so you can stop and resume.

## Notes on reproducing exact paper numbers

Every metric this notebook prints is computed live from whatever's in your
`corpus/` and `benchmark/benchmark.csv` — nothing is hardcoded. Section 6 includes
the paper's published Table 3 as a markdown reference table so you can compare your
run against it, not as a substitute for actually running the pipeline.

Expect small variation from the paper's exact numbers if you:
- use a different corpus subset or a different generation model,
- run generation at a non-zero temperature (this notebook defaults to `0.0`),
- OCR a different set of low-yield pages than we did (tesseract version /
